hq_source: Form 5500 plan sponsor name filed under the payee's own EIN (data/f5500_participants.csv, scripts/07_f5500.py); JobsOhio monthly metrics reports, data/commitments_norm.csv; https://news.google.com/rss/search?q=%22Detroit+Manufacturing+Systems%22+Faurecia+Rush+ownership (Automotive News, Crain's Detroit)
emp_source: Form 5500 plan sponsor name filed under the payee's own EIN (data/f5500_participants.csv, scripts/07_f5500.py)
notes: The payee is a subsidiary vehicle of Detroit Manufacturing Systems, LLC: the Form 5500 for the payee's EIN is filed by Detroit Manufacturing Systems, LLC of Michigan (908 participants in 2015, 1,050 in 2019), and JobsOhio's metrics record the Toledo project under the longer name. DMS itself was a joint venture formed in 2012 between Andra Rush's Rush Group of Detroit and Faurecia of France, and Automotive News reported on August 8, 2018 that Rush sold her stake and stepped down, just after the FY2018 grant year closed on June 30, 2018. I could not document which partner held the majority in FY2018, so the top of the chain is not fully settled; both candidates leave the band at 500-4999 and neither is Ohio, so no published number moves.

name: Speedway LLC

name: AMERICAN REGENT INC
acquired_date: 1991 (Sankyo acquired Luitpold Pharmaceuticals and its subsidiary American Regent Laboratories), 32 years before the FY2023 grant
hq_source: https://www.americanregent.com/our-company/; https://daiichisankyo.us/who-we-are; https://www.americanregent.com/our-business/
emp_source: https://www.daiichisankyo.co.jp/corporate/about/outline/ (20,171 employees, as of March 31, 2026)
notes: American Regent's own Our Company page says "American Regent, Inc. is a proud member of the Daiichi Sankyo Group," every page footer reads "A Daiichi Sankyo Group Company," and Daiichi Sankyo's US site names Daiichi Sankyo Co., Ltd. of Tokyo (TSE 4568) as the parent company. The company's own history page dates the ownership: Sankyo bought Luitpold Pharmaceuticals and its subsidiary American Regent Laboratories in 1991, Sankyo and Daiichi merged in 2005, and in January 2019 American Regent, Inc. merged into Luitpold, which took the American Regent name. That is 32 years before the FY2023 grant, so the ownership is not a later event. Daiichi Sankyo's corporate outline reports 20,171 employees across 32 countries. This moves the record from New York and 500-4999 to Japan and 5000+; it does not touch the Ohio column.

name: Matalco Realty Inc
acquired_date: about 2005 (Giampaolo built and grew Matalco, per its CEO in July 2023), ten years before the FY2015 grant; Rio Tinto bought 50% in December 2023, eight years after it
hq_source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/863064/000162828023026410/ex07d21giampaolojv.htm (Rio Tinto EX-99.7, 21 July 2023); https://www.matalco.com/about/the-giampaolo-group/
emp_source: https://www.matalco.com/about/the-giampaolo-group/ (Giampaolo Group headcount 2,500+)
notes: Rio Tinto's July 21, 2023 notice to the ASX and LSE, filed with the SEC, says it will acquire a 50% stake in "Giampaolo Group's wholly-owned Matalco business," and Giampaolo Group's CEO is quoted saying the group has "grown the Matalco business over the past 18 years," which puts Giampaolo's ownership back to about 2005, ten years before the FY2015 grant. Matalco's own site lists Giampaolo Group Inc. with its headquarters in Brampton, Ontario and a headcount of 2,500 or more, and names Lordstown, Ohio among Matalco's plants. The Rio Tinto joint venture closed in December 2023, eight years after the grant, so it does not change the FY2015 answer. Said plainly: the Giampaolo ownership of Matalco is documented in an SEC filing, but the link from the payee Matalco Realty Inc. to Matalco Inc. rests on the matching name and the Lordstown address, not on a document, which is why this is graded B. The repo's own site-developer re-check reached the same reading. This correction moves $500,000 out of the Ohio column, so it is the one in this batch that most needs a second look.
